issues.body:
gui.yml:553/556 add `--features hdt,federation,odrl,custom-protocol` to the `tauri-build` job. That job has no frontend step: checkout -> Linux webkit apt -> rustup -> cargo cache (path `gui/src-tauri/target` only) -> clippy/build/test -> federation -> odrl -> the new pair. `gui/app/out` is gitignored (gui/app/.gitignore:3) and does not exist in a fresh checkout.

`custom-protocol` sets tauri's codegen out of dev mode (gui/src-tauri/Cargo.toml documents this: tauri's build.rs computes `cfg(dev) = !custom_protocol`). `tauri::generate_context!()` at gui/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:93 then embeds `frontendDist: "../app/out"` (gui/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json) at compile time and fails when that path is missing. This is precisely why every other custom-protocol compile in the repo is preceded by a frontend export: gui.yml:659-661 states it as a requirement ("the shell's `cargo build` embeds whatever is in `gui/app/out` at COMPILE TIME ... so the frontend MUST be built first") before gui.yml:685, and release.yml builds gui/app/out at :376-378 before the bundle at :432.

Consequence: the clippy step fails, the test step at gui.yml:556 never runs, and `hdt` remains compiled in zero CI lanes — the round-1 finding is not actually fixed. The failure is silent: the job is `continue-on-error: true` (gui.yml:457) and its name carries `advisory`, so `ci-summary / gate` ignores it.

Caveat on confidence: I could not execute the build in this environment (tauri-codegen is not vendored/cached and there is no network), so this is derived from the repo's own documented compile-time invariant, not an observed failure.
issues.fix_hint:
Cheapest correct fix: drop `custom-protocol` from the new lane in the `tauri-build` job — that feature only controls asset embedding and has no interaction with the hdt/federation/odrl code paths:

      - name: Clippy (desktop release features, -D warnings)
        run: cargo clippy --all-targets --features hdt,federation,odrl -- -D warnings
      - name: Test (desktop release features, native lane)
        run: cargo test --features hdt,federation,odrl

If you specifically want the full four-feature combination compiled, put that build in the `tauri-e2e` job instead, which already exports gui/app/out before its `cargo build --features custom-protocol` (gui.yml:672-685) — e.g. change that line to `--features hdt,federation,odrl,custom-protocol`. Alternatively add the wasm + `(cd gui/app && npm run build:tauri)` steps to `tauri-build`, but that adds npm+wasm cost to all five OS rows.

Whichever you pick, run the lane once (push a no-op change touching gui.yml so the path filter fires) and confirm it is green before updating release.yml's ledger.
issues.title: New release-feature lane enables `custom-protocol` in a job that never builds `gui/app/out` — compile fails before any coverage is gained

issues.body:
release.yml:420-424 asserts: "The exact plain-Cargo release feature set (`hdt,federation,odrl,custom-protocol`) is clippied and tested on Linux in gui.yml", and :425-426 upgrades the Linux bullet to "the GUI crate feature build + webkit deps are proven green in gui.yml".

Both statements are false as of this diff. The lane they point at cannot compile (see the gui.yml blocker), so nothing in the release feature set is clippied, tested, or proven green anywhere. Even setting the compile failure aside, the lane has never executed yet, so "proven green" is a prediction, not a status — and this block is explicitly the workflow's PROVEN vs DOCUMENTED-UNTESTED honesty ledger, where an unverified claim is exactly the defect it exists to prevent. The round-1 minor ("ledger silent about unproven status") has become an affirmative overclaim, which is worse.

Secondary: the release step now enables three features whose combined effect on the RELEASE profile (`lto = true`, `codegen-units = 1`, gui/src-tauri/Cargo.toml) is still first-compiled on a tag; the gui.yml lane is a debug build. Worth one honest word in the ledger.
issues.fix_hint:
Fix the lane first, observe it green, then state only what is true. Suggested wording:

  #   * The release feature set minus `custom-protocol` (`hdt,federation,odrl`) is clippied and
  #     tested (debug) on Linux in gui.yml's advisory `tauri-build` job; the four-feature
  #     combination WITH `custom-protocol` is compiled in gui.yml's `tauri-e2e` job.
  #     Both are debug builds — the release profile (lto, codegen-units=1) is first exercised here.

and revert the Linux bullet to a claim the evidence supports (e.g. "the GUI crate build + webkit deps are proven green in gui.yml; this feature set is covered by an ADVISORY lane, and the .deb/.AppImage bundle step is the new surface"). Do not restore "proven green" for the feature build until the lane has actually run green at least once.
issues.title: Ledger now claims coverage the added lane does not currently provide ("clippied and tested" / "proven green")

issues.body:
The `tauri-build` job is `continue-on-error: true` (gui.yml:457) and its name embeds `advisory`, which per the job header (gui.yml:442-445) makes `ci-summary / gate` exclude the whole leg. So the feature state the desktop release now depends on is compiled in a lane that can never fail CI — a regression in the shipped feature set would show up only as an ignored red row.

This matches the placement round 1 suggested (next to the existing federation/odrl lanes), so it is not a new defect in kind. It matters here because release.yml:420-426 leans on this lane as the evidence for a load-bearing claim; "proven green" is more than a non-gating, ignore-on-failure lane can support.
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) say so in the release.yml ledger — "covered by an ADVISORY (non-gating) gui.yml lane" — so the reader knows the strength of the evidence, or (b) if the release now depends on this state, promote at least the Linux rows of `tauri-build` to gating (sq-var9 already tracks promoting this leg) or move the release-feature clippy/test into a small non-advisory Linux-only job.
issues.title: The new lane sits in an advisory, `continue-on-error` job excluded from `ci-summary / gate`

issues.body:
The single hdt test, gui/src-tauri/src/engine.rs:539-552 `hdt_import_in_a_lean_build_fails_loudly_with_a_rebuild_hint`, is gated `#[cfg(not(feature = "hdt"))]`, so it is compiled OUT in exactly the state this lane runs. The feature-ON path — `load_hdt` calling `sparq_hdt::load(path)` and `to_loaded_document` (engine.rs:336-341) — gets a type check from the clippy step but is executed by no test.

So the step's name overstates what it covers for hdt: it is a compile lane with the federation/odrl tests attached, not an hdt test. (Enabling all three features also compiles out the `cfg(not(feature = ...))` stub tests for federation and odrl, but those remain covered by the single-feature lanes above.) This was a "consider" in round 1; it is now worth doing because release.yml cites this lane as coverage.
issues.fix_hint: Add a positive hdt test in gui/src-tauri/src/engine.rs under `#[cfg(feature = "hdt")]`: write a small fixture `.hdt` (or reuse one from crates/sparq-hdt's test data) and assert `load_approved_path(..., "hdt", ...)` returns a LoadedDocument with the expected quad count and `format == "hdt"`. Alternatively rename the step to "Build (desktop release features)" so the name does not imply hdt behaviour is tested.
issues.title: `Test (desktop release features)` exercises zero hdt code — the only hdt test is `#[cfg(not(feature = "hdt"))]`

issues.body: The `tauri-build` job now compiles default, `federation`, `odrl`, and `hdt,federation,odrl,custom-protocol` on macos-14, macos-15-intel, ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-24.04-arm and windows-latest, with `timeout-minutes: 45` (gui.yml:458). The new permutation is the heaviest — it links sparq-hdt plus sparq-policy, sparq-solid and the ureq/rustls stack in one unit — and each distinct feature set is a fresh set of cargo units, so the cache key (`gui-tauri-${{ matrix.label }}-${{ hashFiles(...Cargo.lock) }}`) does not help the first run. The Windows row is the likeliest to brush the timeout.
issues.fix_hint: If runs start timing out, restrict the release-feature lane to the Linux rows (`if: runner.os == 'Linux'`) — that matches what the release.yml ledger claims anyway ("clippied and tested on Linux") — or raise `timeout-minutes` for this job.
issues.title: Fourth full feature permutation on five OS rows under a 45-minute timeout

verdict.summary:
Round 2 moves in the right direction on both round-1 majors: `odrl` is now enabled in the release build (making gui/src-tauri/Cargo.toml's "The desktop release build turns it ON" true again, with `forms` explicitly deferred in the new comment), and a CI lane was added to gui.yml to compile/test the shipped feature set. The honesty ledger was also updated, and the round-1 nit about tauri-cli's `--features` additivity is addressed by pinning `custom-protocol` in the plain-cargo lane.

But the new gui.yml lane cannot pass as written, so the round-1 root problem (`hdt` compiled nowhere in CI) is still unresolved, and the release.yml ledger now asserts coverage that does not exist.

The `tauri-build` job (gui.yml:455) never builds the frontend static export: its steps are checkout -> apt -> rustup -> cache (`gui/src-tauri/target` only) -> clippy/build/test -> federation -> odrl -> the new lane. `gui/app/out` is gitignored (gui/app/.gitignore:3) and absent from a fresh checkout. Enabling `custom-protocol` flips tauri's codegen out of dev mode, and `tauri::generate_context!()` (gui/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:93) then embeds `frontendDist: "../app/out"` at COMPILE TIME and hard-errors when that directory does not exist. Every other place in this repo that compiles with `custom-protocol` builds `gui/app/out` first and says so explicitly (gui.yml:659-661 "the shell's `cargo build` embeds whatever is in `gui/app/out` at COMPILE TIME ... so the frontend MUST be built first", then gui.yml:685; release.yml:376-378 then release.yml:432). The new lane at gui.yml:553 omits that prerequisite. Because it is the first step of the pair, the test step at gui.yml:556 is skipped too, and the job is `continue-on-error: true` (gui.yml:457) and advisory-excluded from `ci-summary / gate`, so the failure is silent.
